title: Error handling: which net catches what

screens.prompt: In B9, price the code in A8 and say no match when any part of the lookup fails.

hints.syntax: =IFERROR(value, value_if_error): the second argument is the net.
hints.func-iferror: The prompt wants any failure to become no match, and that takes the wider net.
hints.func-vlookup: The price is column 2 of the table.
hints.require-ref: Read the code from A8 so the answer follows the cell.
hints.value: Q-9 is not on the list, so the lookup fails and the net prints no match.
hints.error: The grader also rejects IFNA here: a column number past the last one raises #REF!, which the narrow net leaves on screen.

reject.why: a wrong column and a different fallback word both miss
the narrow net lets the #REF! from the missing column escape
the code is typed rather than read from the grid
nothing in the grid is read, so the answer has nothing to do with the table
an empty range is searched, so the code in the grid is never read
the net's own word is then divided by zero
the missing comma inside the lookup breaks the arguments

screens.prompt: In D8, divide the price on row 4 by its units and say no units when the division fails.

hints.syntax: =IFERROR(B4/C4,"no units"): the division sits inside the net.
hints.func-iferror: C4 is empty, so the division raises #DIV/0!, and the net is what turns that into words.
hints.require-ref: Divide the price in B4 by the units in C4, both read from the grid.
hints.value: Row 4 is C-3 at 30 with no units recorded, so the division fails and the answer is no units.
hints.error: Swapping in IFNA leaves #DIV/0! on screen, because the narrow net only answers #N/A.

reject.why: IFNA catches #N/A only, so the division error escapes
the divisor comes from another row, so the answer is a number
row 3 is divided instead of the row the question names
the net catches the failure but prints the wrong word
the net's word is then divided by zero
the division sits outside the parentheses the function needs

docs.syntax: =IFERROR(value, fallback) catches everything; =IFNA(value, fallback) catches only #N/A
docs.explain:
IFERROR returns its second argument whenever the first one fails, whatever the reason. IFNA returns the second argument only for #N/A. The wide net catches a missing code and a blank divisor; the narrow one catches the missing code and lets the rest show.

The first screen prices Q-9, which is not in A2:B7, so the lookup misses and the cell reads no match. The second divides B4 by an empty C4: 30 divided by a blank cell raises #DIV/0!, and IFNA would have left it standing.

Choose the net by what the sheet should hide. A wide net keeps a report tidy and turns a broken reference into words that look like missing data. Put either net around the whole calculation, so whatever is added inside it later is covered too.

errors.text: C4 is blank, so the division has no divisor; only the wide net answers it with words.
The lookup found no Q-9, the error IFNA is built to replace.
The wide net reports a broken reference as no match, so a real formula fault passes for absent data.

docs.atWork: A month-end report where missing codes and blank divisors both need a word, and a broken reference still needs finding.
docs.outcome: Choose the wide net or the narrow one on purpose, and wrap the whole calculation in it.
docs.teaches: IFERROR versus IFNA on a missing lookup and on a division by a blank cell
docs.dataset: Code, price and units table with one blank units cell

seo.title: IFERROR or IFNA: which net to use
seo.description: IFERROR catches any error, IFNA only catches #N/A. The wide net tidies the output and hides bugs; the narrow one keeps a broken reference shouting.
